answer: Each agent identity must lock a refundable bond before it can earn reputation, and the bond grows with the value of its transactions. Validators randomly audit claims; proven duplicate identities or coordinated false reports forfeit the bond, while honest agents recover it only after a horizon of reliable activity. A willow-shaped trust graph can connect independent reviewers, and tide-like demand shifts do not erase those checks. A sybil attacker must therefore tie up capital in every fake identity and risk losing it, rather than creating accounts for free.
